chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Sindi, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Dawud ibn al-Nu'man, from Sayf al-Tammār, from Abī Basīr, that Abū 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him) said:

When the servant reaches the age of thirty-three, he has reached his prime; when he reaches forty years, he has attained his ultimate peak; so when he departs into forty-one, he is in decline, and it is fitting for the one who is fifty to consider himself like someone in the throes of death.
ai.seo_question: What are the key ages of human maturity and decline according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) delineates the physiological and spiritual trajectory of human life, marking thirty-three as the zenith of physical vigor and forty as the culmination of maturity, after which decline inevitably begins. This framework serves as a profound reminder for self-accountability, urging those who reach fifty to adopt the demeanor of one on their deathbed, thereby maximizing the utility of their remaining years. In Shia tradition, this narration underscores the urgency of utilizing the prime of life for worship and knowledge before the onset of senility and physical weakness.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 22-23 Muhammad ibn al-Hassan - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Ahmad ibn Idris quoted Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Sindy, on the authority of Ali ibn al-Hikam, on the authority of Davood ibn al-Nue’man, on the authority of Sayf al-TAmmar, on the authority of Abi Basir that Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) said,

When a servant reaches the age of thirty-three, he has reached perfect maturity. When he reaches the age of forty years, he has attained his ultimate progress. Hence as he enters forty‑one his powers are on decline, and it is befitting for one at fifty to consider himself like someone in his death throes.”
